text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment options include lifestyle changes, oral and injectable medications, and sometimes insulin or surgery.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, oral and injectable medications, and sometimes insulin or surgery

list.snippet: Healthy diet: Eat a balanced meal plan rich in lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, and high-fiber whole grains.
Physical activity: Get at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week, plus resistance training.
Weight management: Lose weight if needed to help lower blood sugar and improve overall health.
Glucose monitoring: Check your blood sugar regularly as directed by your care team.
Metformin: The most common first-line oral medicine that lowers glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.
GLP-1 receptor agonists: Injectable drugs (like Ozempic or Victoza) that help release insulin, slow digestion, and support weight loss.
SGLT2 inhibitors: Pills that help remove extra sugar through urine and protect the heart and kidneys.
Sulfonylureas: Oral drugs that prompt the pancreas to make more insulin.
Other oral options: These include DPP-4 inhibitors, TZDs (thiazolidinediones), and meglitinides.
Insulin therapy: Injections or pump delivery used when oral medications and lifestyle steps do not control blood sugar enough.
Bariatric surgery: Weight-loss procedures that can significantly improve or even put type 2 diabetes into remission.
